newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaha to launch cheaper power-bicycle.
newsitem.headline: Yamaha to launch cheaper power-bicycle.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co Ltd said on Monday that it would introduce a new, cheaper electric power-assisted bicycle in Japan next year.
The new bicycle will go on sale on January 15 with a sales target of 100,000 units for calendar 1997.
Its price will be 87,800 yen, which is 49,200 yen cheaper than that of its predecessor.
Yamaha sold 51,000 power-assisted bicycles in calendar 1995 and forecast 1996 sales at 53,000 units.
Its major competitor Honda Motor Co Ltd sold 36,320 units in 1995 and forecast sales of 60,000 units for 1996.
Yamaha's new bicycle will be able to run for 30 kilometres for one power re-charge for ordinary use, longer than the 20 km for the previous model.
It also reduced the time required for recharging the battery to 3.5 hours from 4.5 hours for its predecessors.
